harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and applied the transactional SQLite v1→v2 migration on node1. The catalog remains healthy after a full node reboot, with the original IDs/descriptions preserved, prices initialized to zero, and the original OS/kernel retained.
actions_performed: Replaced bin/upgrade.py with an atomic, repeat-safe migration using BEGIN IMMEDIATE and rollback on any exception.
Added price_cents as INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (price_cents >= 0).
Updated schema_version only after schema alteration and validation succeed.
Applied the migration and verified repeated execution leaves the database unchanged.
Simulated a failure during the version update and proved the complete schema change rolled back to a readable and writable v1 database.
Removed all temporary test and rollback files.
Restarted node1 safely and verified service, security-control, file, and database recovery.

evidence.summary: Final script shows the schema alteration and validation preceding schema_version update, with commit last and rollback on exceptions.

evidence.requirement: Preserve IDs/descriptions, initialize prices to zero, enforce nonnegative values, and reach v2
evidence.summary: Live database passed integrity checking; rows remained (1, Paper) and (2, Tape), both with price_cents=0; negative values were rejected; version is 2.
Both isolated and live reruns succeeded, with identical database hashes before and after the repeated run.

evidence.requirement: Leave v1 usable if the upgrade fails
evidence.summary: A forced failure during schema_version update rolled back the ALTER TABLE, retained version 1 and original data, passed integrity checking, and allowed a v1 write.

evidence.requirement: Clean, secure final state and persistence
evidence.summary: Temporary artifacts were removed. After reboot, SELinux remained enforcing, firewalld and SSH were active, no units were failed, file ownership/labels were intact, and catalog integrity/data/constraints remained healthy.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 2db46909-a020-4fda-b1db-2c3ead04c18a; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID was b05410a1-fdf1-4c53-8e8b-e40c4bb11ff7; full system and catalog recovery were then verified.
